name: Barossa

climate: Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: Australia's Geographical Indications nest in three levels: zones, the regions inside them, and subregions inside those.

notes: Barossa Shiraz, often from old vines, is big and full bodied, with rich chocolate and spice.
Barossa Grenache is jammy and intensely fruity.
Eden Valley, the cooler, rockier part of the zone, is known for Riesling with a lime note.

blurb.text: A South Australian zone made up of two regions, Barossa Valley and Eden Valley. Shiraz is 60 percent of plantings, with Cabernet Sauvignon at 14 percent and smaller shares of Grenache and Riesling.
